passage:
Community Garden Update

To neighborhood volunteers:

The garden committee meet every second Saturday, and volunteers is asked to arrive by nine. At the March workday, forty-two people prepared the beds for spring planting. The group planted tomatoes peppers and beans in the sunny plots, while lettuce and herbs went beside the tool shed. Please check the posted map before adding seedlings so that each crop has enough room.

The new water barrels, which was donated by two local shops, are already full. Because the weather was unusually dry, therefore the team changed the watering schedule. Plot leaders will water on Monday and Thursday mornings, and they will post a notice if heavy rain makes a visit unnecessary. Each volunteer should bring their own gloves, a hat and sunscreen. Drinking water and basic hand tools will be available near the north gate.

The committee wants to thank everyone who have helped so far. Volunteers repaired three raised beds, cleared the accessible path, and labeled the compost bins. Those labels matter because plastic ties and produce stickers must be removed before plant scraps are added. A coordinator will give new volunteers a short composting demonstration at 9:15.

Families are welcome, but an adult must supervise children near the tool shed and water tanks. The south path will remain open for neighbors who want to visit without joining the work crew. Please keep wheelbarrows and hoses away from that path.

Next month we will repair the fence we will also add two shaded benches. The fence work will begin near the alley, where two loose boards have allowed rabbits into the garden. The bench locations were chosen after several visitors explained that the nearest public seating is across a busy street. Anyone interested in the carpentry team should list that experience on the sign-up form.

Please sign up by the Thursday before each workday. Early registration helps the coordinators prepare tools, drinking water, and task cards. If rain forces a cancellation, the committee will send a text by 7:30 Saturday morning and post the same message at the gate. Questions may be sent to the volunteer coordinator through the contact form on the garden's website.
